name: Error Handling
description: 3-layer error hierarchy, Result<T,E> type, RFC 7807 HTTP mapping, React error boundary
checklist: Return Result<T, E> (src/shared/result.ts) from use cases that can fail expectedly; throw only for programmer/config errors
Wrap infrastructure failures as err(new ExternalServiceError(...)), then wrap at the application boundary (UseCaseError) so lower layers don't leak upward
Use handleError(error, instance) in routes/middleware: Next.js → Response.json(body, { status }); Express → res.status(status).json(body)

If you generated the React boundary: wrap top-level trees with <ErrorBoundary> in app/layout.tsx, and swap its componentDidCatch console.error for your observability logger if the observability template is installed
If you enabled Sentry: npm install @sentry/node, merge .env.sentry.example into .env.local, set SENTRY_DSN (the handler then reports unhandled errors automatically)
